algorithm.Title: Measles Exposure - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Measles contact/exposure assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published measles guidance's contact-tracing recommendations.
algorithm.Author: IST Health Open-Source Guideline Content
algorithm.LastRevised: RESEARCH_REQUIRED - internal IST clinical adaptation date is not recorded

questions.Question: Is a widespread rash the main concern rather than contact with a person who may have measles?
questions.Information: A widespread rash belongs in the Rash or Redness - Widespread pathway.

questions.Question: Has the person had close contact with someone with measles and is unvaccinated or only partially vaccinated, pregnant, under 1 year old, or has a weakened immune system?
questions.Information: NHS.UK measles guidance recommends urgent clinical contact for these groups after measles exposure - measles in pregnancy can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, or premature birth, and infants/immunocompromised people are at higher risk of severe disease.

questions.Question: Has the person had 2 doses of MMR vaccine or measles before, with none of the higher-risk factors above?
questions.Information: Fully vaccinated or previously infected individuals are generally protected and can monitor at home for symptoms.

advice.Title: Urgent measles exposure follow-up
Content: Contact the Qatar urgent clinical review pathway promptly - do not simply walk into a clinic, as measles is highly contagious and the clinic may need to prepare to see you safely.
Call Back If: fever or rash develops.

advice.Title: Governed Qatar measles-exposure monitoring
Content: Do not attend a clinic unannounced. Avoid contact with infants, pregnant people, and immunocompromised people, and contact the Qatar public-health/clinical route approved by governance to verify exposure, immunity, vaccination records, and whether time-sensitive post-exposure action applies. Monitor for fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and spreading rash; call ahead before any in-person care. Vaccine or immunoglobulin eligibility/timing must not be invented by UAT content.
Call Back If: fever, cough, red eyes, or rash develops; breathing difficulty, dehydration, confusion, seizure, or severe illness.

references: NHS.UK, "Measles", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/measles/ (page last reviewed 31 July 2025) - contact-tracing/exposure guidance section

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What is the exposed person's exact age and sex, are they pregnant or immunocompromised, when/where/how close was contact, who confirmed measles, and what vaccination or prior-immunity evidence exists? Include infant and safeguarding concerns.
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 22 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Has the person had 2 doses of MMR vaccine, or had measles before?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 22 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: Is the person pregnant, under 1 year old, or immunocompromised?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Condition-relevant assessment retained from the cited Batch 22 source.

initialAssessmentQuestions.Question: What has a safe parent or caregiver observed about alertness, breathing, pain, swelling, fever, eating or drinking, sleep, play, and normal activity?
initialAssessmentQuestions.Rationale: Child assessment adds safe-caregiver observations without inventing a different clinical threshold.
